title: Present Continuous
subtitle: What are they doing now?
goals: I can say what people are doing now.
I can use am, is and are + -ing: I am playing, she is playing, they are playing.
I can say I'm not, isn't and aren't.
I can ask Is …? and Are …? and answer Yes / No.
I can name sports things and places: ball, bat, hoop, goal, racket, net, gym, field, court, pool.
teacherGoals: Present Continuous for actions happening now (now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!).
am / is / are + verb-ing; -ing spelling: + ing, e goes, double the last letter.
Negatives: I'm not / am not, isn't, aren't + verb-ing.
Am / Is / Are questions, short answers (Yes, she is. / No, they aren't.), What are you doing?
teacherNote: This week follows Compass Unit 2 (“Why do we play sports?”): Sports Things and Places (p. 28) + Present Continuous (p. 29). Book words: balls, bat, hoop, goal, racket, net, gym, field, court, pool. All -ing forms come from a checked list. Learn 12 compares Week 1 (every day) and Week 2 (now).

dashboard.tagline: Let's talk about what is happening now!

learn.title: Now! Look! Listen!
learn.rule: We use am / is / are + -ing for things that are happening now.

examples.text: Mia **is reading** a book **at the moment**.
examples.label: at the moment = now

examples.text: Look! Leo **is running** in the park.

practice.explain: Shh! It is happening now: is sleeping.

learn.teacherNote: Signal words: now, at the moment, right now, Look!, Listen!, Shh! Ask “Is it happening now?” before every sentence.

learn.title: I am, you are, he is …
learn.rule: I → am. He / she / it → is. You / we / they → are.

examples.speaker: Sam
examples.label: Sam is talking to Mia. you → are

learn.teacherNote: This is the same am / is / are pupils know from “I am happy.” Now it is a helper: am / is / are + -ing.

learn.title: He / she / it + is + -ing
learn.rule: He, she, it (one person or thing) + is + verb-ing.
learn.teacherNote: Two parts every time: is + verb-ing. Pupils often forget one part (“He swimming.” / “He is swim.”). Point to both blocks in the machine.

learn.title: I am / you, we, they are + -ing
learn.rule: I + am + verb-ing. You / we / they + are + verb-ing.

practice.explain: Sam and Leo = they → are playing.

learn.teacherNote: Short forms are fine and common in speaking: I'm, you're, we're, they're. The site accepts both “I am” and “I'm”.

learn.title: playing, riding, swimming
learn.rule: Look at the end of the verb before you add -ing.

examples.text: Leo is run**ning** in the park.
examples.label: run → running (double n)

learn.teacherNote: All forms come from a checked list. Short verbs with one vowel + one consonant double the last letter (run, swim, get, put, hit, sit). Verbs ending in -e drop the e (ride, write, dance, have). play, fly: just + ing.

learn.title: He / she / it + isn't + -ing
learn.rule: He, she, it + isn't (is not) + verb-ing.

examples.text: Sam **isn't** sleeping. He is playing football.
Mia **isn't** watching TV. She is reading.
Ana **isn't** walking. She is riding a bike.
Leo **is not** swimming. He is running.
examples.label: is not = isn't

learn.teacherNote: The -ing stays after isn't. Compare Week 1: “He doesn't play” (no -ing) and Week 2: “He isn't playing” (with -ing).

learn.title: I'm not / you, we, they aren't
learn.rule: I + am not ('m not). You / we / they + aren't (are not) + verb-ing.

examples.text: I**'m not** sleeping! I am reading.
examples.speaker: Sam
examples.label: I'm not = I am not

examples.text: We **aren't** watching TV. We are reading.
examples.speaker: Mia

examples.text: Sam and Leo **aren't** playing football. They are playing chess.

learn.teacherNote: There is no short form “amn't”. Pupils can say “I'm not” or “I am not”.

learn.title: Is he …? Are they …?
learn.rule: Put am / is / are first. The -ing verb stays.

examples.label: Mia is reading. → Is Mia reading?

learn.teacherNote: No do / does in these questions! “Does she playing?” is a common mix-up after Week 1.

learn.title: Yes, she is. / No, they aren't.
learn.rule: Is she playing? Yes, she is. No, she isn't.

practice.prompt: Ms. Rosa asks Ana: “Are you drawing?” Ana is drawing. Ana says:
practice.explain: Ana talks about Ana: Yes, I am.

learn.teacherNote: Short answers use only am / is / are — no -ing: “Yes, she is.” not “Yes, she is playing.” (that is a full answer, also fine in speaking).

learn.title: What are you doing?

examples.q: Where are Mia and Sam running?

practice.explain: Sam = he → What is Sam doing?

learn.teacherNote: A very useful classroom question: “What are you doing?” Use it all week with real actions in class.

learn.title: Book words: ball, bat, hoop, goal …
learn.rule: Sports things and places from the book (Unit 2, p. 28).

examples.text: Leo is hitting the ball with a **bat**.
Ana is throwing the ball into the **hoop**.
Sam is kicking the ball into the **goal**.
Mia is playing tennis with a **racket**.
Leo and Ana are playing volleyball over the **net**.
Mia and Ana are doing exercises in the **gym**.
Sam and Leo are playing basketball on the **court**.
Mia and Sam are running on the **field**.
Mia and Sam are putting the **balls** in the basket.

practice.prompt: Mia is playing tennis with a ___.

learn.teacherNote: Things: balls, bat, hoop, goal, racket, net. Places: gym, field, court, pool. Ask “Where …?” for places and “What is he using?” for things.

learn.title: Book words: do gymnastics, go skating …
learn.rule: Sports and activities from the book: do, play, go … + -ing.

examples.text: Mia and Sam **are running a race**.
examples.label: run → running (double n)

practice.explain: do karate → Leo is doing karate.
go skating → Sam is going skating.

learn.teacherNote: Compass Unit 2 vocabulary “Sports and Activities”. Point out the verb partners: do gymnastics / karate, play baseball / tag, go skating / swimming.

learn.title: Story words: a good game
learn.rule: Action words from the reading “A Good Sport”, in our own sentences.

examples.text: Look! Sam **is running across the field**.
Sam **is kicking the ball** … Goal! He **is scoring a goal**!
Mia and Ana **are cheering** for the team.
Now Sam and Leo **are giving high fives**.

practice.prompt: Mia and Ana ___ for the team.
practice.explain: Mia and Ana = they → are cheering.

learn.teacherNote: Read the book story first. These sentences reuse its action words (score a goal, pass, kick, cheer, shout, give high fives, win) in Present Continuous.

learn.title: Every day or now?
learn.rule: Every day → plays (Week 1). Now → is playing (Week 2).

examples.text: Pepper **doesn't** go to school. Now it **is sleeping**.

learn.teacherNote: Every day, every Saturday, on Mondays → Present Simple. Now, at the moment, Look!, Listen! → Present Continuous.

practice.prompt: She is singing. Which is the question?
They are running. Which is the negative?

learn.teacherNote: Same three moves every time: + (am / is / are + -ing) · − (add not) · ? (am / is / are goes first).

speaking.question: Every day or now? Say two sentences about Sam.
speaking.sample: Sam plays football every Saturday. Now he is playing football.

speaking.question: What is Mia doing?
speaking.sample: She is doing gymnastics.

speaking.question: Is Leo playing baseball or doing karate?
speaking.sample: He is doing karate.

speaking.question: Mime a sport! Your friends ask: “Are you going skating?”
speaking.sample: Are you going skating? Yes, I am!

speaking.question: Look at the game. Who is cheering? Who is scoring a goal?
speaking.sample: Mia and Ana are cheering. Sam is scoring a goal.
